【I'll share the lot calculation tool I've been using lately♪】

When you look at charts and trade day after day, I think what everyone finds a hassle is lot calculation.

Both on my YouTube and in my PDF teaching materials,

I've said "I calculate with this site's calculator~"

and I shared one convenient free calculation tool in the past,

but it can't be denied that it has these drawbacks:

*Every calculation takes time.

*It's a pain to type in the entry and stop-loss values each time.

*If you make a typo, the lot size goes off and risks causing an unexpected loss.

*So you worry about whether it's really correct and often have to double-check.

It's fine when the scenario has been clear for several hours and you have time before entry, but when you want to enter right away you get flustered, don't you?

And when you're flustered, mistakes are more likely to occur, which is a vicious circle.

If you have no time before entry yet the calculation is bothersome, you can't concentrate on chart analysis either, so misjudgments are also more likely.

So after searching around, I found an extremely convenient calculation tool, and I'm using it now.

It's a tool called "Easy Order". (This links to my blog article.)
↓
https://t.co/rIqMKqNjE0…

I explain it in detail in the blog too, but what's convenient is that you don't have to enter numbers and calculate each time; you just slide three horizontal lines for entry, stop-loss and take-profit up and down on MT4!!

Just by moving the lines up and down by feel, like "the stop-loss should be around here, I'll enter around here," it automatically calculates the appropriate lot size!

And you can place market, limit and stop orders with one click!

Using this, you can find the appropriate lot size in seconds without any tedious calculation, so deciding the lot before entry becomes revolutionarily easy♪

The risk-reward ratio is also displayed automatically.

It's a god-tier tool that instantly solves all the stress, hassle, complexity, and anxiety about making mistakes that you've had with lot and risk-reward calculations until now.

It also supports overseas FX brokers like XM, which I use, as well as CFDs and crypto instruments other than currencies.

So you don't need to split it up like using this tool for currencies and another tool for crypto.

Admittedly it isn't free, but the price of 4,500 yen is quite reasonable, which is also appealing.

Considering that you're freed from the hassle of lot calculation every time, and that with a single purchase lot and risk-reward calculations will be easier from now on, I think it's definitely a good deal.

Looking at X, quite a few people who trade with the same method as me are already using this tool.

https://t.co/rIqMKqNjE0…

Without exaggeration, you'll be freed from all the hassle of lot calculation, it becomes tremendously easier, and you'll be able to concentrate only on chart analysis.

I really recommend it to those who struggle with lot or risk-reward calculations or feel they're bad at them, so I'll quietly share it on a Friday night. 😁

In Japan it's all lumped together as "overseas FX", but FX is fundamentally a global
financial business.
In the UK there's INFINOX, in Australia IC Markets, and Exness and ATFX also have entities and bases in multiple countries, operating around the world.
In 2023 ATFX acquired Rakuten Securities Australia, and the following year it switched to the ATFX brand.
Every country has its own FX brokers, and on top of that, while following each country's rules,
they expand their business overseas too.
Japan has domestic FX companies too, and that's fine.
But why does Japan separate domestic and overseas so much?
I understand investor protection is needed,
and I don't take that lightly, but regulating and closing off the market are different things.
Rather than just protecting the domestic market,
I think we could consider an environment where people can properly use the world's financial services under proper
rules, competing with the world.
Not toward closing, but toward connecting with the world.
That's what I think🦅
